intro: Physician assistants make clinical decisions every day, so their closest matches are in teaching and research. The closest of the 25 careers below is Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary, with a 71% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $107,310, which is 21% less than the $135,880 physician assistants earn.
why_it_works: A clinic day means examining patients, ordering tests, prescribing and explaining plans clearly. O*NET rates judgment, service orientation and social perceptiveness at 4 out of 5 for this job. Teaching, genetic counseling, clinical research and health informatics draw on the same depth of knowledge. Because your pay is already high, only 2 matches pay more. The gaps are instructing groups and programming.
tips: Teach in a PA program or precept students first to test academic work.
Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, which is 9% more, and are a 67% match.
Health informatics suits PAs who enjoy data, with a median of $105,850 for its broader group.

faq.q: What jobs can former physician assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are postsecondary health specialties teachers (71%), Genetic Counselors (71%) and Medical Dosimetrists (67%), based on O*NET 31.0. Clinical research coordinators are also 67% matched, with a median of $167,220 for their broader BLS group, and keep you close to patient care.

faq.q: Which careers for physician assistants pay more?
faq.a: Only 2 of the 25 matches pay more than $135,880. Industrial-Organizational Psychologists earn $193,950 (43% more) and Medical Dosimetrists $147,470 (9% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Psychology requires its own graduate training, while dosimetry has certificate programs.

faq.q: Do physician assistants need another degree to switch?
faq.a: No for all 25 matches: each usually needs no more education than physician assistants already have. A master's degree is common, held by 91% of workers in a close match, so your PA degree covers most formal requirements, although some research roles prefer extra training.

faq.q: What skills should physician assistants build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are instructing, operation and control, coordination and programming. Complex problem solving already rates 3.88 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so teaching and technical skills are the main steps outside clinical practice.
